title: Classic Space Game Wing Commander 3 Is Getting a Remaster
summary:
Fans of classic computer games got a big surprise this weekend. At the Portland Retro Gaming Expo, a large event for people who love older video games, an Electronic Arts producer announced that Wing Commander 3: Heart of the Tiger is getting a remaster. A remaster is a new, improved version of an older game.

Wing Commander was a popular series of space flight games on PC computers in the 1990s. The series had five main games, a dozen expansions, books, an animated show and even a movie. But it has mostly been left alone since around the year 2000.

During a panel looking back at the series, producer Jim Vessella said he had found the original master tapes from the making of Wing Commander 3. One fan who was there posted that Vessella found more than 600 source tapes in the company's archives and has been restoring them.

Vessella told the crowd that a 30th anniversary remaster is on the way. The video scenes will be cleaned up, and the game will run at 60 frames per second, which makes motion look smoother. It will also include improvements made by fans after the game came out, plus "the Kilrathi Saga," which suggests the first three games may be included.

In the game, players fly as a space pilot named Christopher Blair in a war between humans and the Kilrathi, an empire of giant cat-like aliens. The game is famous for its live-action movie scenes starring real actors, including Mark Hamill, who played Luke Skywalker in Star Wars.

Kotaku, which reported the news, noted that the reveal was a little unusual, since Vessella did not work on the original series. The series' creator, Chris Roberts, now leads a different space game called Star Citizen.
why_it_matters: Remasters let new players experience classic games and help preserve gaming history that might otherwise be lost. Finding old master tapes can save the original work for the future.
